mainTopic: Combining half-כזית intentions (slow eating, unusual food, eating vs. burning), and the new פרק on שחיטה by unfit people
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's proof from the משנה: if two people are each meant to eat half a כזית, the two halves combine. רבא then asks whether intent to eat a כזית slowly, over more than כדי אכילת פרס, still counts. Is it like the מזבח's burning, which has no time limit, or like a person's eating, which does? אביי tries to prove there is no limit, but the גמרא answers that the משנה may mean a big fire that burns fast. Next the גמרא finds an apparent contradiction between two clauses of the משנה about food that is not normally eaten. רבי ירמיה says the later clause follows רבי אליעזר. אביי says the whole משנה follows the רבנן if we read the inference as being about normal food. The גמרא then shows why the eating-and-burning clause is still needed. The פרק ends with a הדרן, and a new משנה teaches that unfit people's שחיטה is valid, so their wrong intent can disqualify the קרבן.

steps.title: Two people eating half each do combine
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his inference from the משנה. Eating plus eating, set up like eating plus burning (two separate 'eaters'), does combine. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if the intent was to eat and to eat, set up like 'to eat and to burn'. What case is that? Two people. Then the halves combine! Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a proof from the משנה. It shows that when someone intends for two different people each to eat half a כזית, the two halves add up to a full כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says eating and burning don't combine. That implies eating and eating would combine. Since 'eating and burning' involves two different consumers (a person and the מזבח), the matching 'eating and eating' case must be two different people. So two people's halves join, and the question is settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together / combines into one full amount
What is the case? How does it look?
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Intent for two people to each eat half a כזית combines into a full כזית of disqualifying intent.

phrases.english: But if the intent was to eat and to eat
set up like 'to eat and to burn'
and what is that case? With two people
phrases.notes: Eating and burning means two consumers, a person and the מזבח. So the matching case is two different eaters.

phrases.english: it combines! Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל דּוּמְיָא דְּלֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun on the previous amud, answering whether two people's half-כזית intentions combine.
steps.raayaObject: Whether intentions for two different people to each eat half a כזית combine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: eating half a כזית and burning half a כזית is כשר because eating and burning don't combine.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two people's half-כזית eating intentions do combine.

steps.title: Does a very slow eating still count?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about intent to eat a כזית over more time than אכילת פרס. Is it judged like the מזבח's burning, with no time limit, or like human eating, which has one?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if he intended to eat a כזית over more than the time of eating a half-loaf, what is the law? Do we compare it to the eating of the Most High, or to the eating of a regular person?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. Does an intention to eat a כזית of a קרבן very slowly still count as a real 'eating' intention?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular person, eating a כזית spread over more than כדי אכילת פרס is not counted as one act of eating. But the מזבח 'eats' by burning, and that can take as long as it takes. רבא asks which model applies to eating קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount that counts
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf; the window for counting one eating
The Most High: the מזבח's 'eating', meaning burning

phrases.english: Rava asked
If he intended to eat an olive's volume
over more than the time of eating a half-loaf, what is the law?
Do we compare it to the eating of the Most High
phrases.notes: That means burning on the מזבח, which has no set time limit.

phrases.english: or do we compare it to the eating of a regular person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that builds on the same topic of what counts as a disqualifying eating intention.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does intent to eat a כזית over more than כדי אכילת פרס count, by comparison to the מזבח's burning (no limit) or to human eating (limited)?

steps.title: אביי's proof that there is no time limit
steps.stepSummary: אביי uses the משנה. Eating combines with an eating set up like burning, and burning a כזית can take longer than אכילת פרס. So there is no time limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: come hear. 'To eat half a כזית and to burn half a כזית is כשר, because eating and burning don't combine.' The reason is that it was eating and burning. But eating and eating does combine. And burning takes more than the time of eating a half-loaf!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to answer רבא's question from the same משנה. He argues that slow eating does count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'eat and eat like eat and burn' inference is read differently. The second half is eaten at the slow pace of burning. Since that still combines, and burning takes longer than כדי אכילת פרס, eating קדשים must be judged like the מזבח's eating, with no time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid; the קרבן is not disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: The same inference from the משנה ('eat and eat combines') was used in step 1 to talk about two people. Here אביי uses it in a new way: one eating happens at the slow speed of burning.

phrases.english: Abaye said: come and hear

phrases.aramaic: לֶאֱכוֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת – כָּשֵׁר
phrases.english: to eat half an olive's volume and to burn half an olive's volume: it is valid
because eating and burning do not combine
The reason is that it was to eat and to burn
but to eat and to eat combines
phrases.notes: אביי reads the second 'eating' as happening at the slow pace of burning.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הַקְטָרָה בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס הוּא!
phrases.english: And burning takes more than the time of eating a half-loaf!

steps.raayaObject: That eating קדשים has no maximum time, like the מזבח's eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An inference from the משנה about eating and burning half a כזית each.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה means a big fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה may be talking about a large fire, which burns the half-כזית within the time of אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is with a large fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed burning always takes longer than כדי אכילת פרס. But with a big fire, the half-כזית burns quickly, inside the normal eating window. So the משנה proves nothing about slow eating, and רבא's question stays open.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof is rejected. Burning can be fast with a big fire, so רבא's question about slow eating is not answered here.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is with a large fire.
phrases.notes: A big fire burns the piece fast, within the half-loaf eating time.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; it does not decide רבא's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed burning always takes longer than כדי אכילת פרס, but a large fire burns within that time.

steps.title: Inference from the eating-and-burning clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that eating half a כזית plus burning half a כזית does not combine, and infers that eating plus eating combines even when the second half is something not normally eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he intended to eat half a כזית and to burn half a כזית, the offering is fit. The reason is only because it was eating plus burning. But eating plus eating, even of something not normally eaten, would combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a line of the משנה closely and draws a conclusion from what it leaves unsaid. This sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה blames the failure to combine on the mix of 'eating' and 'burning'. So if both intentions were about eating, they should combine, even if one half is something people don't usually eat. Notice how far this inference reaches: it includes unusual food.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive-bulk, half the minimum amount that counts
Combines, joins together to make a full amount
The reason is; it opens an inference from the wording

phrases.english: To eat half an olive-bulk
and to burn half an olive-bulk – it is fit.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. The intent here is to do these things after the proper time or outside the proper place.

phrases.english: The reason is that it was to eat and to burn,
but if it was to eat and to eat
something not normally eaten – it combines.
phrases.notes: He means: half a כזית of the regular meat, plus half a כזית of something people don't usually eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר, הָא לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new inference from the same משנה, now about which kinds of items can combine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the wording: eating plus eating combines, even when one half is something not normally eaten.

steps.title: The first clause says only normal food combines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference using the רישא, which implies that only things normally eaten combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part of the משנה teaches: intent to eat something normally eaten combines. That means normally-eaten things, yes; things not normally eaten, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two parts of the same משנה seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא makes a point of saying 'something normally eaten combines', which implies that unusual items do not combine. But the inference from the סיפא in step 5 said unusual items do combine. Both can't be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
But it teaches; it introduces a contradicting source

phrases.english: But the first clause teaches:
to eat something that is normally eaten – it combines;
something normally eaten, yes,
something not normally eaten, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the inference of step 5 against an inference from the רישא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that eating plus something not normally eaten combines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא implies the opposite: only normally-eaten items combine. So the two clauses of the משנה contradict each other.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the later clause follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the inference from the later clause follows רבי אליעזר, who counts intent even for things not normally eaten or burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Whose view is this? It is רבי אליעזר, who says intent counts when moving from human eating to the מזבח's eating, and from the מזבח's eating to human eating. As we learned: if someone slaughters an offering intending to eat something not normally eaten, or to burn something not normally burned, it is fit. And רבי אליעזר disqualifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה resolves the contradiction by saying the two clauses follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, intent about an unusual item is real intent, so it can combine with intent about regular meat. The רבנן disagree, and the רישא follows them. The proof is another משנה where רבי אליעזר disqualifies in exactly this kind of case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא is willing to split one משנה between two opinions to remove a contradiction.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the inference from the later clause, the one in step 5.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מְחַשְּׁבִין מֵאֲכִילַת אָדָם לַאֲכִילַת מִזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: who said: one can have intent from human eating to the altar's eating,
phrases.notes: For example, planning to burn on the מזבח a part that people normally eat still counts as real intent.

phrases.english: and from the altar's eating to human eating.
phrases.notes: And the other way around: planning to eat a part that normally goes on the מזבח also counts.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who slaughters the offering
intending to eat something not normally eaten,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְהַקְטִיר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לְהַקְטִיר – כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: or to burn something not normally burned – it is fit.
And Rabbi Eliezer disqualifies it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two clauses to different תנאים (רבנן and רבי אליעזר).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses of the משנה follow one opinion, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא follows the רבנן; the inference from the later clause follows רבי אליעזר, who counts intent about unusual items.

steps.title: אביי: read the inference about normal food
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the whole משנה can follow the רבנן. The inference from the later clause should be read as talking about two halves of normally-eaten food.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say it follows the רבנן. Don't infer 'eating plus eating of something not normally eaten combines.' Rather, infer 'eating plus eating of something normally eaten combines.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He keeps one opinion for the whole משנה and fixes the inference instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction only came from reading the inference too broadly in step 5. If the inference is only about two halves of normal food, it agrees with the רישא. Then there is no need to bring in רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say it follows the רבנן
And do not say (do not infer this way)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the contradiction: רבי ירמיה splits the משנה between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר; אביי keeps it all as the רבנן and narrows the inference to normal food.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not changing the words of the משנה. He is only changing what we infer from it.

phrases.english: Abaye said: You can even say it follows the Rabbis
and do not say: but to eat and to eat
something not normally eaten,
rather say: but to eat and to eat
something normally eaten.
phrases.notes: So both halves are regular food, and they combine. This fits the רישא perfectly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction than רבי ירמיה gave in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the inference so it no longer contradicts the רישא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inference included things not normally eaten, which clashes with the רישא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inference only says that two halves of normally-eaten food combine. The whole משנה follows the רבנן.

steps.title: If the clause teaches about normally-eaten food, the first clause already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's reading. If the later clause only teaches that two halves of normally-eaten food combine, we already know that from the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the clause teaching us? If it teaches that halves of something normally eaten combine, we can learn that from the first clause. Half a כזית outside its place plus half a כזית tomorrow is פסול. That implies half a כזית tomorrow plus half a כזית tomorrow is פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the later clause adds if we read it the way אביי does. Its first option is that the clause adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the later clause hints that two halves of normally-eaten food combine. But the רישא already shows this. Mixed intents (outside + tomorrow) only make the קרבן פסול, which implies two 'tomorrow' halves combine into a full פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asking what a statement adds)
The first clause of the משנה
Disqualified (but without the extra penalty of פיגול)
A קרבן ruined by intent to eat it after its allowed time

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
phrases.notes: "It" is the later clause of the משנה, read the way אביי explained it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן –
phrases.english: If it teaches us about something that is normally eaten,
learn it from the first clause:
half an olive-bulk outside its place
and half an olive-bulk the next day: it is disqualified.
This implies that half an olive-bulk the next day [with another half the next day] makes it piggul!
phrases.notes: If both halves were planned for 'tomorrow,' they would combine into a full כזית and make it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? אִי דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reading of the later clause by asking what it adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the later clause teaches that halves of normally-eaten food combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That point is already implied by the רישא, so the later clause would be extra.

steps.title: If the clause teaches eating plus burning, a קל וחומר already teaches it
steps.stepSummary: Second option: the clause teaches its plain meaning, that eating plus burning does not combine. But the רישא implies even eating plus eating something not normally eaten fails to combine. So eating plus burning surely doesn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it teaches that eating and burning don't combine, learn it from the inference of the first clause. Intent to eat something normally eaten counts; intent to eat something not normally eaten does not. Now, if eating plus eating something not normally eaten does not combine, do we need to be told about eating plus burning?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other way to read the clause and shows that this reading also seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא implies that intent to eat something not normally eaten doesn't count at all. That case is still just 'eating' and it fails to combine. So eating plus burning, two totally different acts, should fail all the more (a קל וחומר). Either way, the later clause looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: An inference drawn from the exact wording
Combines (two halves joining to make a full amount)

phrases.english: Rather, if it teaches about intent to eat and to burn,
learn it from the inference of the first clause:
intent to eat something normally eaten: yes, it counts;
something not normally eaten: no.
Now, if intent to eat and to eat

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל – לָא מִצְטָרֵף,
phrases.english: something not normally eaten does not combine,
is it necessary to say that eating and burning don't combine?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי לֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר מִדּוּקְיָא דְּרֵישָׁא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by covering the second possible reading of the clause.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the later clause: eating plus burning does not combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the רישא's inference already proves it. If eating plus eating something not normally eaten doesn't combine, eating plus burning surely doesn't.

steps.title: Eating plus burning was needed, since each half follows its normal way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the eating-and-burning case was needed. In the רישא's case the problem may be the unusual eating. But here each half is planned in its normal way, so one might think they combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eating and burning had to be taught. I might have thought: there, it doesn't combine because he plans to eat something in an unusual way. But here, one half is planned in its normal way and the other half in its normal way, so say they combine. The משנה teaches us they don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משנה. The eating-plus-burning case teaches something the קל וחומר could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר breaks down. The eating-and-eating case may fail only because one half is eaten unusually. In eating-and-burning, the food is planned for eating and the burnable part for burning, so both are normal. That might have made it combine, so the משנה had to say it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Has intent (forms a plan in his mind)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה needs the eating-and-burning case. Without it, we might think two intents combine when each half is planned in its normal way. The משנה teaches they still don't combine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves אביי's approach: the whole משנה can follow the רבנן, and no clause is extra.

phrases.english: The case of eating and burning was necessary;
it might have entered your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּלָאו כִּי אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מְחַשֵּׁב;
phrases.english: there, it doesn't combine because he plans to do it not in its normal way;
phrases.notes: "There" is the case of eating plus eating something not normally eaten.

phrases.english: but here,
where with this half it is in its normal way
and with that half it is in its normal way,
I would say they should combine;
so it teaches us that they don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר אִיצְטְרִיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר from step 10 by showing why it fails.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Breaking the קל וחומר (צריכותא: showing the clause was needed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating plus burning might combine, since each half is planned in its normal way, unlike the unusual eating in the רישא's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when each half follows its normal way, eating plus burning does not combine.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of כל הזבחים שקבלו דמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the פרק called כל הזבחים שקבלו דמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'כל הזבחים שקבלו דמן'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק. It tells us the discussion of this chapter is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula is said at the end of every פרק. It names the chapter by its opening words, and it shows our love for the learning and our hope to come back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the closing formula said at the end of a פרק
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter about a קרבן whose blood was received with wrong intent or by unfit people is now complete. A new topic starts next.

phrases.english: We will return to you
"All offerings whose blood was received"
phrases.notes: This is the name of the chapter, taken from its first words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ דָּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole chapter after the discussion in step 11 ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק כל הזבחים שקבלו דמן is finished.

steps.title: Slaughter by unfit people is valid
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that when people unfit for עבודה slaughter a קרבן, the שחיטה is valid. The one condition is that a טמא person may not touch the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All unfit people who slaughtered a קרבן: their slaughter is valid. This is because שחיטה is valid when done by a זר, by women, by slaves, and by טמאים. This is true even for קדשי קדשים, as long as the טמאים do not touch the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It teaches that שחיטה of a קרבן does not need a fit כהן; anyone may slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of the עבודה, like receiving and sprinkling the blood, must be done by a fit כהן. שחיטה is different: it is valid even by a זר, a woman, a slave, or a טמא person. The only limit is practical: a טמא person must not touch the meat, because he would make it טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit to do the עבודה in the מקדש
Offerings of the holiest level, like a חטאת or עולה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a טמא person's שחיטה is פסול just because he is טמא. The שחיטה itself is valid; he only has to be careful not to touch the meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets שחיטה apart from the other main עבודות, which need a fit כהן. That difference is the basis for the next line about intent.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All unfit people who slaughtered
their slaughter is valid,
because slaughter is valid
by non-priests and by women
and by slaves and by impure people.
And even with offerings of the most sacred order,
as long as the impure people do not
touch the meat.
phrases.notes: If they touched it, the meat would become impure. That is the only problem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַפְּסוּלִין שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ שְׁחִיטָתָן כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה of a קרבן is valid even by people unfit for עבודה, even for קדשי קדשים, as long as a טמא person does not touch the meat.

steps.title: Their wrong intent can disqualify the offering
steps.stepSummary: Because their שחיטה counts, these unfit people can also make the קרבן פסול through wrong intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, they disqualify the קרבן with their intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws a result from the rule it just taught. Since the unfit person's שחיטה is a real שחיטה, his thoughts during it matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrong intent, like planning to eat the קרבן after its time (פיגול) or outside its place, can ruin a קרבן only when it is held during a valid עבודה. Here the unfit person's שחיטה is valid, so his מחשבה counts and can make the קרבן פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore: a result that follows from what was just said
Intent during the עבודה, such as planning to eat the קרבן after its time or outside its place

steps.whatToRemember: An unfit person's שחיטה works fully, both for good and for bad. It makes the קרבן valid, and his wrong intent during it can make the קרבן פסול.

phrases.english: Therefore, they disqualify
with intent.
phrases.notes: This means wrong intent during the slaughter, like planning to eat the offering after its time or outside its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a result from step 13: because their שחיטה is valid, their intent during it also counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfit people who slaughter can make the קרבן פסול through wrong intent, because their שחיטה is a valid עבודה.
